slides.headline: A 13-YEAR-OLD CHROME BUG COULD READ ALL YOUR FILES
THE AI CAUGHT TWO YEARS OF BUGS
slides.body: Google built it with Gemini in early 2026. By March, it had more reports than all of 2025. By June, it passed two full years

slides.headline: ONE BUG HID FOR 13 YEARS
slides.body: It could've let hackers read files off your laptop: photos, passwords, everything. It survived in Chrome's code for 13 years before the AI caught it

slides.headline: THE AI HUNTS WITHOUT INTERNET
slides.body: It runs on locked-down machines with zero internet. It can only touch the code it's told to test, nothing else. A caged hunter

slides.headline: EACH BUG COST 30 MINUTES OF HUMAN TIME
slides.body: Checking one bug report took a human 5 to 30+ minutes. If Google needs AI to protect its own browser, nobody's code is safe without it

slides.headline: THIS AI GETS SMARTER EVERY MONTH
slides.body: Follow and watch what it catches next. Send this to the friend who still thinks their passwords are safe

caption:
Swipe to see how Google's AI exposed Chrome's worst security holes in a single month 🔓

Google's Gemini-powered AI bug hunter, two years of Chrome bugs caught in one month, a 13-year-old flaw that could've let hackers read your photos and passwords, locked-down machines with zero internet, 5 to 30 minute triage times replaced by AI, what this means for every business running software.

Google just proved that AI catches what humans can't, and the gap is only growing. If the biggest tech company on Earth needs AI to protect its own browser, the rest of us are already behind.
